bull_bear.body: Deliberate deleveraging alongside bolt-on M&A: **net debt ₹1,110mn (0.06x)** with a commitment to **fully repay outstanding debt during FY27**, cutting finance cost further (already a driver of PAT more than doubling since FY24). **₹9,674mn cash** on hand described as flexibility for strategic initiatives. **Adjusted ROCE >50%**, **cash conversion ~70%**. M&A is capability-led, disciplined on valuation (**RCM targets passed on price**), and structured so that CareSeed's 31.4% EBITDA margin business is **accretive to margin**, not dilutive. A **~3% ESOP pool** is approved-in-process but ungranted — a future, unquantified P&L charge.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
1. **Q2 absorbs the full minimum-wage impact — "more than double" Q1's 40bps** — against a 24–25% guide that is already partly FX-funded.
2. **The margin defence relies on currency.** If the rupee reverses, the 120bps has nothing to lean on but efficiency, which takes **12–18 months**.
3. **Hedges taken at lower rates** mean **reported** EBITDA/EPS will not enjoy the FX benefit that flatters adjusted EBITDA.
4. **No pricing power at all** — stated outright. Growth must come entirely from volume, scope and new logos while clients push prices *down*.
5. **AI deflation is guided to rise from 100–150bps to ~200bps and "maybe even go higher"** — a permanent, self-inflicted revenue headwind inherent to the model.
6. **Client concentration is increasing**, not decreasing — *"if you can see the percentage of our top three, top five, they also continue to increase"* — even as 55+ mid-market clients were bought in.
7. **A top-5 cohort is shrinking** on an onshore→offshore migration. Margin-positive, revenue-negative, and it will recur.
8. **Managed-service deals take 3–6 months of conversation**; the shift to outcome-based revenue is real but slow, and effort-based pricing still dominates.
9. **Only 1 new logo** in Q1's $35.3mn ACV — growth is overwhelmingly farming, not hunting.
10. **Adjusted vs reported gap is wide** (earnouts, SARs, intangible amortisation, the ₹151mn exceptional, the one-time wage item). Every headline metric on this call is an adjusted one.
11. **Open-enrolment volumes unknowable until September** — the single biggest determinant of H2, and management said so.
12. **Peers are reportedly seeing payer spending tighten**; Sagility says it is not, *"at least we are not seeing in the conversations that we are having."* Watch for divergence.
13. **The ~3% ESOP pool** is an unquantified future dilution/charge.
14. **CareSeed's platform may not scale to large payers** — management conceded most large clients already have quality-reporting vendors; only a packaged platform+services play could enter.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Unusually disciplined disclosure. They gave a **quantified margin bridge in basis points**, split the minimum-wage hit into its in-quarter (₹70mn) and exceptional (₹151mn) components, disclosed the **exact geographic exposure (65–70% of headcount)** that makes the shock large, admitted the FX crutch when asked directly (*"Both, right? Currency has played a part"*), and volunteered the adjusted-vs-reported hedge distinction unprompted. They **refused to raise guidance three times** off a 14.9% CC organic quarter, and refused to extrapolate 5.1% sequential growth (*"I wouldn't read too much into it"*). Two answers were "we'll come back to you" (the FY26-cohort growth split; BroadPath revenue), which for a company that has now made two acquisitions is a fair ask to follow up. The one moment of edge — *"Baidik, you're asking the same question multiple ways"* — read as conviction rather than irritation. Overall this is management being **structurally conservative into a strong quarter**, which is the right posture ahead of a full-quarter wage hit.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The Everest data point — 70% of payers have "adopted AI", only 10% see measurable improvement — is the single most valuable disclosure on the call.** It reframes AI from a threat to a BPM's addressable problem: piecemeal AI fails, end-to-end workflow redesign is required, and only a domain-deep operator can do that redesign.
- **Insourcing is economically impossible for cost-pressured payers** because the work sits offshore. Cost pressure on clients is therefore a *tailwind*, not a risk — the exact inverse of the usual outsourcing-cycle worry.
- **Sagility has zero pricing power and is growing 15% CC anyway.** All of it is volume/scope. That is a stronger signal about demand than any pricing-led beat would be.
- **The margin guide is being defended with FX, and management said so.** The underlying operating margin is *not* comfortably absorbing 120bps yet — mitigation is 12–18 months out.
- **Deliberate geographic de-risking has begun** — Indore, Tamil Nadu, Mumbai — driven not by cost arbitrage but by **regulatory wage risk concentration** in Karnataka/Telangana. Expect this to become a structural cost line.
- **CareSeed is tiny ($5.1mn) but bought at 31.4% EBITDA margin with 95% recurring revenue and 26 new logos** — the client list and the Medicare-Advantage quality capability are the assets; the revenue is rounding.
- **Seasonality doubled (3% → 6% of revenue) because of BroadPath**, and is now a permanent feature of the Q1 and Q2 optics. Sequential declines in Q1 are structural, not signals.
- **Attrition improving from 38.1% to 28.6% in one quarter** is a large, under-discussed cost and quality tailwind in a 47,307-person business.
- **Present in only 7 of the top 10 national insurers, and entry to the rest must come through clinical and payment integrity** — the traditional claims/enrolment work at those accounts is already placed elsewhere. That is a precise, checkable roadmap.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Deleveraging is the stated priority: net debt fell from ₹21,678M in FY24 to ₹10,433M in FY25, ₹1,962M in FY26 and ₹1,110M at TTM Jun26, with the deck noting "Debt to be fully repaid in current Financial year" (FY26 closing debt ₹5,670M, FY27 debt repayment ₹5,670M, interest payment ₹287M in FY27 and nil thereafter).
- Adjusted ROCE (Adjusted PAT plus interest cost divided by capital employed excluding goodwill and intangibles, less current liabilities) was 58.6% at TTM Jun26, versus 47.0% in FY24, 54.9% in FY25 and 58.9% in FY26.
- Cash conversion: "Q1 FY27 Cash Conversion at 69.9% impacted by acquisition-related earnout payments"; OCF on reported EBITDA was 69.9% in Q1 FY27 (64.7% FY26) and FCF on reported EBITDA 53.4% (54.4% FY26), with DSO of 80 days.
- Dividend paid was ₹234M in FY26 and nil in Q1 FY27; committed future outflows disclosed include earnout costs of ₹64M in FY27, ₹95M in FY28 and ₹19M in FY29 (FY27 relating to BroadPath and CareSeed; FY28–FY29 CareSeed only).
- The balance sheet at 30 Jun 26 is goodwill-heavy: goodwill ₹65,591M and other intangible assets ₹20,515M against total assets ₹127,884M and equity ₹99,265M, with borrowings ₹5,777M and lease liabilities ₹5,114M.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Exclusive, 26-year specialization in U.S. healthcare operations spanning payer, provider and pharmacy workflows - domain intensity in areas that are difficult to commoditize
- Long-standing, deeply embedded client relationships reflected in high retention; five largest client groups had an average tenure of 18 years as of 31st March 2026
- Scale and franchise depth - serves more than 80 healthcare client enterprises and seven of the top 10 U.S. healthcare payers by enrolment
- Global delivery footprint across five countries with over 46,000 professionals including clinicians and technology specialists, enabling execution at scale
- AI-embedded operating model (System of Intelligence + System of Orchestration and Action) applying explainable, compliant decision intelligence directly inside workflows rather than as a standalone tool
- Outcome-based engagement structures that align Sagility's success with client results, shifting relationships from transactional execution to shared ownership of outcomes
- Broadening client mix - 17 new clients added in FY 2026 including regional Blues plans, reducing top-client concentration and adding resilience
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Total dependence on a single end-market: the entire revenue base comes from the U.S. healthcare industry, with exports contributing 100% of turnover — Exposes Sagility to U.S. regulatory, economic and outsourcing-related developments - healthcare policy shifts, proposed measures such as the HIRE Act and state-level anti-outsourcing bills. Mitigations cited: deepening presence across both payer and provider segments, expanding into adjacent higher-value areas such as clinical services and pharmacy benefit management, regulatory-compliance and information-security focus, a multi-country delivery footprint (U.S., Jamaica, Colombia onshore/nearshore; India and the Philippines offshore) and negligible dependency on H1B visas.
- Client concentration and client restructuring - the top 10 client groups contribute 83.9% of total revenue — Consolidation, mergers, acquisitions or restructuring among healthcare payers and providers may cause vendor rationalization, contract renegotiation, volume reallocation or pricing pressure. Mitigations: diversifying across payer and provider segments, scaling end-to-end RCM in providers, higher-value clinical/patient-support offerings for PBMs and specialty pharmacy, multi-year performance-linked contracts, the BroadPath-led entry into mid- and small-market accounts, and proactive engagement during client M&A.
- Fluctuation in client business volumes, including the risk of clients insourcing work — Revenues are linked to client-driven transaction volumes that can swing with membership trends, cost pressures, regulatory change, outsourcing decisions or client reprioritisation, affecting revenue predictability, capacity utilization and operating leverage. Mitigated through diversified revenue streams, flexible operating models, multi-year and outcome-based constructs, dynamic workforce management, cross-trained talent and multi-geo scalable delivery, plus platform integration that raises client dependence and reduces insourcing likelihood.
- Competitive intensity and pricing pressure from global outsourcing providers, broad-based IT/business services firms, specialised healthcare-focused companies and clients' own in-house/digital capabilities — Competition combined with client cost-efficiency focus drives evolving commercial constructs and pricing dynamics. Sagility responds with an integrated domain-led operating model, a shift to outcome-based and managed-services constructs (value-led rather than price-led), non-linear output-based commercial models, expansion into higher-value clinical and adjacent lines, geo-shifts/multi-shore cost optimisation, and regular monitoring of account margins with periodic reporting to leadership.
- Cybersecurity and data privacy - handling sensitive protected health information across a partly remote workforce — Data breaches or non-compliance with stringent U.S. and global data-protection regimes (HIPAA, HITECH, CCPA, GDPR) could trigger regulatory action, financial penalties, lost business and reputational damage; delayed incident reporting is itself a compliance exposure. Controls include encryption, identity management, access controls and network protection, periodic risk assessments, vulnerability testing and independent external reviews, privacy impact assessments, data mapping, third-party data-sharing controls, a defined incident-management process owned by Compliance and Cybersecurity, training and awareness, and market-benchmarked cyber insurance.
- Talent management, attrition and wage inflation in a competitive talent market, including key-management succession — Elevated attrition and wage inflation affect service continuity, cost structures and margin profile; permanent-employee voluntary attrition (above 90 days) was 29.4% in FY 2026 versus 27.5% in FY 2025. Loss of senior leaders who hold deep domain expertise and long-standing client relationships could impair client confidence and service continuity. Mitigated through competitive, market-aligned compensation and benefits programmes.
- Regulatory compliance complexity from operating across multiple geographies — Frequent regulatory change increases compliance complexity and multi-jurisdiction operations increase legal exposure; non-compliance may result in penalties, financial strain and reputational damage. Managed through periodic Legal-team oversight, regular compliance status reporting (including exceptions) to Senior Management, the Audit Committee and the Board, and refreshing compliance frameworks as regulations evolve.
- Ethics and integrity / conduct risk — Unethical practices may invite regulatory scrutiny and penalties, and misconduct can damage brand reputation and stakeholder trust, potentially reducing investor confidence and access to financing. Addressed through a formal whistleblower mechanism allowing confidential reporting, with matters reviewed under established protocols and the code of conduct.

bull_bear.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)

business.body:
- **Payer operations (89.6% of revenue):** the core. Growth led by **expansion within existing relationships**, with **FY26-added clients beginning to scale**. No pricing lever was used — see §7.
- **Providers (10.4%):** RCM. Management has looked at RCM acquisition targets and passed: *"a lot of the RCM targets that came out didn't clearly add to our capabilities and the valuations were pretty high."*
- **CareSeed (closed 11-Jun-2026):** Kansas City, founded 2012, **14-person team**, **CY25 revenue $5.1mn at 31.4% EBITDA margin with 95% recurring revenue**, **30 small/mid payer clients (26 new to Sagility)**. Two platforms: **Forecast** (HEDIS reporting & quality analytics) and **Harvest** (cloud-based medical-record review and chart abstraction). The acquisition thesis has four pillars — capability (quality for **Medicare Advantage**: HEDIS, CMS Stars, care-gap orchestration), technology, cross-sell into 26 mid-market clients, and talent with established client relationships.
- **The CareSeed value-chain extension is the important part:** Sagility can attach **chart abstraction** to the platform, **create the chase list**, integrate Forecast/Harvest with its own **population-health AIP platform** (care coach/care manager workflow), and then go beyond identifying care gaps to **closing** them via member outreach and behavioural change — *"health plans can move beyond HEDIS reporting to member level orchestration, while unlocking star improvement and revenue uplift."*
- **BroadPath:** ~**$13.5–13.6mn** in Q1, now fully merged — *"it's very difficult to say, is it a BroadPath client or a Sagility client, right? It's a combined team now."* It is the main reason seasonal revenue doubled from ~3% to ~6% of the total (Medicare sales and enrolment support).
- **Sagility Synchrony:** AI-led orchestration platform connecting fragmented claims and adjustment workflows — *"making inroads"*, no revenue disclosed.
- **A top-5 client cohort is going backwards for a good reason:** a large line of business is being **migrated from onshore to offshore delivery**, which reduces revenue but management confirms is **margin-accretive**.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **The Everest Group finding is the strategic wedge and it is commissioned, first-party evidence** (50 payer decision-makers): **70% claim to have adopted AI, only 10% report measurable improvement**; **70% identify domain-led intelligent operations as a priority**. Management's read: *"people who are doing AI implementation on a piecemeal basis aren't seeing the returns that they expected. So redesigning large part of the workflows end-to-end is very critical before you embark on an agentic implementation of AI."* Domain knowledge, not model access, is the scarce input.
- **Insourcing is structurally uneconomic for clients** — the clearest defensive argument on the call: *"insourcing this work, especially if it's not done in the U.S., if it's done in a different geography, will only increase the cost to the clients. So when they're under cost pressure, that's not the direction that they are likely to go."*
- **Execution scale as a stated strength, not a constraint:** asked whether delivery capacity is the only limit to growth, the CEO replied *"scaling up execution is the least of our concerns... I'm not trying to be arrogant, but we've always executed well"* — the binding constraint is **deal timing**, not capacity.
- **Third-party validation:** major contender in Everest's **Healthcare CXM** and **RCM Intelligent Operations PEAK Matrix 2026**; **Avasant leader** in clinical & care-management business-process transformation (RadarView 2026); **Great Place to Work India #11** in its first year of entering.
- **Attrition improving sharply** (38.1% → 28.6% QoQ) in a labour-arbitrage business where retention *is* the delivery moat.

business.body:
- Revenue is overwhelmingly payer-led: "Revenue by Vertical Split — By Payer %" was 89.6% in Q1 FY27 (89.9% TTM Jun'26) versus "By Provider %" 10.4% (10.1% TTM Jun'26).
- The deck cites third-party validation of the model — Major Contender in the Healthcare CXM Intelligent Operations PEAK Matrix Assessment 2026 and in the Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) Intelligent Operations PEAK Matrix Assessment 2026, and Leader in the Avasant Clinical and Care Management Business Process Transformation 2026 RadarView.
- Sagility-commissioned Everest Group research across 50 payer decision makers is presented as validating demand for its model: "70% have adopted AI; only 10% report measurable improvement", "70% identify domain-led intelligent operations as a priority", "94% expect AI + human oversight" and "84% report limited AI value today".
- Client concentration has fallen steadily: Top 3 clients were 60.1% of revenue on a TTM Jun26 basis versus 72.4% in FY23; Top 10 were 84.1% versus 90.7% in FY23.
- Revenues are described as seasonal: "Our Revenues exhibit seasonality. Q3 & Q4 have seasonal Revenues from Open Enrolment and AEP" — Q1 FY27 carried no seasonal revenue versus ₹2,260M in Q4 FY26.

business.body:
- [Acquisition] CareSeed, "founded in 2012 and headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri", is a US healthcare analytics company with ~$5.1MN CY25 revenue, ~95% recurring revenue, 31.4% CY25 EBITDA margin, 30 small and mid payer clients and 14 team members.

business.title: Competitive strengths

latest_quarter.body:
- **The minimum-wage shock is bigger than the headline suggests** because of pay-parity cascade: *"not only the folks who are on minimum wages get a hike... There's also cascading impact on people to ensure pay parity across. It impacts a larger portion of people than the base associates."* With **65–70% of headcount in Bangalore and Hyderabad**, that cascade is the whole 120bps.
- **Q1 captured barely a third of it** (Karnataka effective 23 May); **Q2 impact is "more than double"**.
- **The offset is candidly part-FX:** *"Currency has played a part and helped us to retain the guidance... But even otherwise, even in the underlying forecast, we had some efficiency initiatives planned."* The CFO added that hedges *"were taken last year at a much lower value"* — so the FX benefit shows in adjusted EBITDA but the hedge drag lands in **reported EBITDA and EPS**. A real distinction investors should carry.
- **Mitigation levers named:** expand delivery into **states outside Karnataka and Telangana** (<15–20% of headcount today), and step up **operational efficiency** — full mitigation **12–18 months** away.
- **NO pricing power — and management says so plainly:** *"There were no pricing levers that we exercised... Given the situation of our clients, the movement in prices is in the opposite direction. So there's more pricing pressure than any price increases that we would get. So there is no revenue growth because of price increases."* **All growth is volume and scope.**
- **Three structural deflation sources**, cumulatively **100–150bps historically, guided toward 200bps**: (1) **onshore→offshore migration** of client work, (2) automation savings shared back with clients, (3) **AI**.
- **Internal AI is deliberately not a headcount story:** it targets support functions — *"Can I hire more efficiently using AI? Can I train people more efficiently... Today, if I'm taking six weeks to get somebody proficient, can I take the help of AI and reduce the training timeline to four weeks?"* Headcount reduction only happens **when a client authorises AI in their process** (illustratively 100 people → 80).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (prior):** adjusted EBITDA margin **24.9%**; open-enrolment revenue **~$24.8mn** in the quarter; voluntary attrition **38.1%**; DSO 87 days; BroadPath still separately identifiable; FY27 guidance of **low double-digit CC organic growth** and **24–25% adjusted EBITDA margin** first set.
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Revenue **₹19,635mn / $207.8mn (+27.6%, +15.2% CC)**; organic **+14.9% CC**; steady-state sequential **+5.1%**. Adjusted EBITDA **₹4,716mn, 24.0%**; adjusted PAT **₹2,697mn (+35.1%), 13.7%**. OCF ₹3,161mn (**~70% conversion**), FCF ₹2,416mn. **DSO 80 (from 87)**; cash ₹9,674mn; **net debt ₹1,110mn / 0.06x**; **ROCE >50%**. Headcount **47,307**; **attrition 28.6% (from 38.1%)**. **$35.3mn ACV** across 18 existing + **1 new logo**. outlook.body:
- **FY27 revenue: low double-digit ORGANIC growth in constant currency — REITERATED**, despite Q1 delivering **14.9% CC organic**. Pressed three separate ways by two analysts, the CEO would not raise it: *"we are still guiding to low double-digit growth... Will it be exactly that number, plus, minus some number? But yes, definitely, we are reasonably confident of delivering the double-digit number."*
- **FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin: 24–25% MAINTAINED**, explicitly *"despite absorbing 120 basis points incremental impact from minimum wage increases in Karnataka and Telangana."* Upside flagged: *"If the eventual outcome on minimum wages results in a lower impact, we could be at the upper end of that range or even higher"*, and separately *"we should do better than the lower end of that range."*
- **Q2 carries the FULL minimum-wage impact** — Q1 captured only ~5 weeks (Karnataka effective **23 May**): *"That itself is almost more than double the impact that we had this quarter."*
- **Narrower guidance promised at the Q2 call (October)**, once open-enrolment/AEP bids are finalised — *"most plans would be finalising their bids by this time... we'll get to know specifics only by September."*
- **Full repayment of all outstanding debt during FY27** — *"We remain on track to fully repay our outstanding debt during FY 2027."*
- **Seasonal revenue to remain ~6% of total in FY27**, same proportion as FY26 (it was ~3% / ~$20mn in FY25, rising to ~$50mn / ~6% in FY26 after BroadPath).
- **Minimum-wage mitigation: 12–18 months** to play out fully, via expansion into states outside Karnataka/Telangana plus operational efficiency.
- **AI-led revenue deflation: historically 100–150bps, guided to ~200bps in the near future and "maybe even go higher"** — not tracked quarterly; a broader read promised next quarter.
- **ESOP pool of ~3% of equity** announced but **not yet granted**; spread over multiple years; P&L impact to be reported in a subsequent call.
- **Not guided / declined:** the split of growth between FY26-cohort and legacy clients (*"I don't have those numbers handy... we can come back to you"*), BroadPath's ongoing revenue split, and any quarterly sequential growth rate (*"The 5% may not continue every quarter"*).

Managed-service/outcome-based deals are in **active conversation for three to six months** each and remain the timing risk (*"deal timing can be difficult to predict"*). Cross-sell pipeline: **six or seven active opportunities in BroadPath clients**; CareSeed cross-sell just beginning. Penetration into the **top 10 US national insurers is 7 of 10** — the remaining three are long-time outsourcers whose traditional work is already placed, so entry must come via **clinical** and **payment integrity**, areas they have not outsourced to the same extent.

outlook.body:
- **Managed-service / outcome-based constructs** — *"we take operational ownership of, and accountability for a large part of the value chain and deliver committed outcomes at a much lower cost."* Still a minority of wins; effort-based FTE/transaction pricing continues alongside.
- **Mid- and small-market expansion** — **55+ mid-market clients** added across BroadPath and CareSeed; cross-sell described as *"pretty high"* opportunity in mid-market, but the CareSeed **platform** is unlikely to sell into large payers (who already have quality-reporting vendors) — only the **combined platform + services package** could.

outlook.body:
- Position Sagility as the decision intelligence and outcomes layer for healthcare operations, combining deep healthcare domain expertise, technology/analytics/AI and operational execution into a single operating model that delivers measurable outcomes
- Shift engagements from effort-based, discrete services toward outcome-based and performance-aligned structures where Sagility takes accountability for client results
- Scale technology and AI-led, platform-enabled solutions - moving beyond task-level automation to redesigning critical workflows as AI-led, orchestrated operating systems with human-in-the-loop governance
- Expand connected lifecycle operating models such as Synchrony across administrative, clinical and financial operations, managing connected workflows rather than isolated processes
- Deepen penetration of existing client relationships while diversifying the revenue base and reducing top-client concentration
- Expand into the mid- and small-market payer segment, leveraging the BroadPath acquisition to broaden reach across client segments
- Pursue selective, targeted acquisitions that complement capabilities, deepen domain expertise and expand technology and AI capabilities
- Deepen capabilities across payer and provider workflows - enrolment, claims, payment integrity, care management, revenue cycle support and engagement operations
- Embed AI into internal processes including hiring, training, quality, coaching and real-time operations management to drive consistency, accuracy, speed and control
- Maintain financial discipline and capital efficiency - prudent capital deployment balancing growth investment with a strong balance sheet and financial flexibility
- In FY 2027, scale with greater emphasis on execution consistency, client outcomes and operational discipline
- The Board declared an interim dividend of Rs 0.05 per equity share of Rs 10 each in October 2025 (paid November 2025) and has recommended a final dividend of Rs 0.10 per equity share of Rs 10 each for FY 2026, both placed for confirmation/approval at the Fifth AGM on 20th August 2026. No formal dividend-policy text, buyback or debt-reduction philosophy statement appears in the governance sections provided; the group's stated governance posture emphasises lawful, ethical and transparent conduct with rigorous oversight of risk management, cybersecurity and regulatory compliance, and Corporate Governance Guidelines applied across Sagility Group entities.
- BRSR disclosures are made on a consolidated basis covering operations in India, the USA, the Philippines, Jamaica and Colombia, with limited assurance on BRSR Core attributes provided by DNV Business Assurance India Private Limited
- Material responsible-business-conduct issues formally identified: Cybersecurity and Data Privacy (risk), Client Satisfaction & Innovation (opportunity), Ethics & Integrity (risk), Compliance (risk), Health, Safety & Wellbeing (opportunity) and DEI (Diversity, Equity...)
- Cybersecurity and data privacy managed through a structured control framework - formal data security policies, procedures and standards, periodic training and awareness, privacy impact assessments, data mapping, third-party data-sharing controls and a defined incident-management process owned by the Compliance and Cybersecurity teams, with ongoing monitoring of regulatory and standard-setting developments
- A global health and safety policy sets minimum requirements for safe and healthy workplaces, supported by site-level practices, periodic incident reviews and root-cause analysis with tracked corrective and preventive actions
- Formal whistleblower mechanism available to employees and other stakeholders as the grievance-redressal route for employees/workers, customers and value chain partners, alongside Investor Relations and Compliance Report channels for investors, shareholders and communities; no complaints were pending resolution for the categories disclosed as Nil
- Gender diversity: the permanent workforce of 46,860 employees as of 31st March 2026 is 61.2% female and 38.7% male, with 0.1% recorded as others; women constitute 22.2% of the Board of Directors, including two women Independent Directors, while women representation among the disclosed KMP is 0.0%
- Workforce attrition disclosed on a voluntary basis (above 90 days): total permanent-employee turnover of 29.4% in FY 2026 versus 27.5% in FY 2025 and 27.2% in FY 2024
- CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013
- Board-level oversight of risk via a Risk Management Committee chaired by an Independent Director, with the Board affirming that in its opinion no risks currently threaten the existence of the Company; the Risk Management policy is published on the Company website
- Board familiarization for Independent Directors includes regular updates on key risk metrics and mitigation strategies, regulatory developments and emerging technology trends including cybersecurity; the Board skills matrix explicitly includes Risk Management, Cybersecurity and Corporate Social Responsibility as required competencies
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Sagility is an asset-light services business, so expansion is expressed as delivery footprint, capability build-out and acquisitions rather than plant capex. The Company delivers services through its tools and platforms and its talent pool from 31 global service delivery locations across India, the Philippines, the U.S., Jamaica and Colombia; the Board's Report notes this multi-geography footprint combines onshore and nearshore locations in the U.S., Jamaica and Colombia with offshore centres in India and the Philippines, a diversified base that reduces dependence on any single country and supports business continuity. Delivery capacity is scaled through people - a workforce of more than 46,000 professionals worldwide, including clinicians and technology specialists - supported by dynamic workforce management, cross-trained talent pools and multi-geo scalable delivery infrastructure that allows capacity to be aligned to fluctuating client volumes. Footprint expansion is also pursued through M&A: the BroadPath Healthcare Solutions acquisition is described as a strategic step towards entering the mid- and small-market segment, broadening the client base and service portfolio, with its integration and contribution extending Sagility's market reach and complementing its service portfolio. Capability expansion is directed at adjacent, higher-value areas - clinical services and pharmacy benefit management, patient support offerings for PBMs and specialty pharmacy players, and scaling end-to-end Revenue Cycle Management within the provider segment - alongside continued investment in AI, platform-led capabilities and integrated operating models that connect fragmented workflows, plus proprietary platform integration inside client workflows to raise switching costs. Cost-side footprint actions include proactive geo-shifts and a multi-shore delivery model to optimise cost structures. Management states that improvements in margins, operational rigor and balance sheet strength have enhanced the Company's capacity to invest with purpose, with investments directed toward initiatives that reinforce competitive advantage. No named plant, site-commissioning or dated capacity-addition project is disclosed in the provided sections.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- U.S. national health expenditure is projected by CMS to reach 20.3% of GDP by 2033, up from 17.6% in 2023, underscoring market scale and the urgency of improving healthcare administration
- Demographic change - the U.S. Census Bureau identifies 2030 as a turning point when all baby boomers will be over 65 and one in five U.S. residents will be of retirement age, driving more frequent and complex healthcare interactions
- Chronic disease burden (diabetes, cardiovascular, respiratory conditions) drives utilization and reinforces demand for prevention, risk stratification, care coordination and population-level interventions
- Medicare Advantage enrolment continues to increase but growth is maturing and profitability pressure is intensifying, pushing plans to invest in AI, automation, operational efficiency, Stars performance, utilization management, payment integrity and member experience
- Medicaid change from post-pandemic eligibility redeterminations plus funding/eligibility/operational changes under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBB), and expiry of enhanced ACA Marketplace premium subsidies - together increasing membership volatility across Medicaid and Exchange populations and demand for enrollment, eligibility, claims, billing, payment integrity and member engagement capability
- Rising consumer expectations for convenience, transparency, speed and personalization, accelerating demand for responsive, digital, experience-led engagement models
- Shift toward value-based care and migration of care to lower-cost outpatient, ambulatory, virtual and home-based settings, increasing the need for coordination across administrative, clinical and financial workflows
- Clients moving away from fragmented vendor relationships and point solutions toward integrated partners - shifting the basis of competition from scale alone to relevance, integration and end-to-end workflow value
- Competitive intensity rising as technology-native firms, platform providers and diversified services players increase presence, raising the bar on speed, interoperability and measurable outcomes
- AI adoption moving from isolated pilots toward enterprise-scale deployment, favouring providers with domain specificity, regulatory awareness, auditability and human judgment in the loop
- Margin levers cited: operating leverage from scale, execution efficiency, an increasing mix of transformation-led and outcome-based engagements, automation and digital workflows, tight control of discretionary expenses, and the ability to scale back excess capacity after the open enrollment season
- Revenue mix remains rooted in the payer segment with the provider segment seen as an expansion opportunity; BroadPath supports member-facing and seasonal operations during peak enrolment cycles
- Management expects the market to keep shifting toward AI-enabled, platform-supported and more integrated operating models, with clients emphasising partners that reduce administrative waste and deliver measurable outcomes at scale
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: A clean beat on every line — revenue **+27.6% (+15.2% CC)**, adjusted EBITDA **+27.9%**, adjusted PAT **+35.1%**, adjusted **ROCE >50%**, net debt down to **0.06x** — delivered while absorbing annual increments *and* a genuinely large statutory shock: **Karnataka and Telangana minimum-wage revisions**, worth **~120bps of FY27 adjusted EBITDA**, hitting a base where **65–70% of headcount sits in Bangalore and Hyderabad**. Management held the **24–25% margin guidance** anyway, explicitly funded by **FX (+100bps in Q1)** plus efficiency initiatives — an honest admission that the offset is partly not operational. The strategic direction is the more interesting story: a shift from *"fragmented process-led models"* to **managed-service deals where Sagility owns the workflow end-to-end and commits to a cost takeout** — underpinned by commissioned Everest Group research showing **70% of payers claim AI adoption but only 10% report measurable improvement**, which is precisely the wedge for an integrator. The most conservative thing on the call: after 14.9% CC organic growth in Q1, guidance stayed at **low double digits**, and the CEO refused three separate invitations to raise it.
